source: Cholera West Africa Risk Factors 1986 AJPH

Data from risk factor study conducted during epidemic in Guinea West Africa.

source: WHO Disease Outbreak News 2001 Guinea Cholera
processing_notes: Source states: '155 cases, including 12 deaths have been reported from 6 August to 23 September in N'zerekore region in the south-eastern part of the country' - interpreted as 155 sCh with 12 deaths. N'zerekore borders Cote d'Ivoire to east and Liberia to south. WHO official outbreak notification.

Source states: 'Guinea had reported 333 cases of cholera and 31 deaths up to 31 Aug 2004' - interpreted as 333 sCh cases with 31 deaths reported to WHO as of August 31 2004. Partial year data from WHO 2004 annual report.

source: Guinea Cholera Safe Water Sources and Sanitations SCIRP
processing_notes: Source states epidemic hit Guinea starting April 2005. OCHA report states 102 deaths among 3797 cases in Moyenne Guinea and Conakry from April-December 2005 with no new cases since November. Interpreted as 3797 sCh cases. Processing note: partial year data, outbreak began April 2005.

source: Guinea Cholera Safe Water Sources and Sanitations SCIRP
processing_notes: Source states: 'From January to July 2006, the Public Health Ministry notified 1,623 cases of which 143 died' - interpreted as 1623 sCh with 143 deaths. ReliefWeb confirmed: report dated August 20 2006 from Guinea Ministry of Public Health via UN OCHA. Partial year data January-July 2006.

source: Feasibility Mass Vaccination OCV Guinea 2012 PLOS Medicine
processing_notes: Source states: 'Guinea experienced a previous major epidemic in 2007 with 8,289 cases and 295 deaths' - interpreted as 8289 sCh with 295 deaths for full year 2007. SCIRP paper on Guinea cholera 2000-2012 corroborates this as major outbreak year within 2004-2008 period.

source: Deciphering Origin 2012 Cholera Epidemic Guinea PLOS NTD
processing_notes: Source states: 'In 2004-2008, Guinea was struck by a succession of regional cholera outbreaks responsible for 17,638 reported cases and 786 deaths' - interpreted as 17638 sCh with 786 deaths aggregate 2004-2008. Processing note: This is a multi-year aggregate covering 5 years. Individual year data available for 2004 (333 cases), 2006 (1623 partial), 2007 (8289). confidence_weight reduced for multi-year aggregate. Do not sum with individual year rows without checking for overlap.

source: Deciphering Origin 2012 Cholera Epidemic Guinea PLOS NTD
processing_notes: Source states: 'A three-year lull period was observed from 2009 to 2011' and 'Investigations found that the lack of cholera during a lull period is not due to inadequate surveillance or laboratory incompetence but simply due to the absence of cholera cases' - confirmed zero-transmission. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from peer-reviewed academic study. Surveillance system status: operational (early cholera alert system established 2009). CFR=0 reflects confirmed zero-transmission period.

source: Deciphering Origin 2012 Cholera Epidemic Guinea PLOS NTD
processing_notes: Source states: 'The 2012 epidemic was officially responsible for 7,350 suspected cases and 133 deaths. CFR: 1.8%' - interpreted as 7350 sCh with 133 deaths. Outbreak started February 2 2012 on Kaback Island Forecariah prefecture (index case fisherman from Sierra Leone). Epidemic ended February 6 2013. National level data.

source: Cholera Incidence AFRICHOL Multi-country Surveillance PLOS NTD
processing_notes: Source states: '34% (4,585) in Conakry, Guinea' of all AFRICHOL study cases. '15 deaths among suspected cases' in Conakry. 55 culture-confirmed cases. CFR 1.2% overall period - epidemic period CFR 0.3%. AFRICHOL enhanced surveillance August 2011-December 2013 in all 5 Conakry districts. Processing note: Conakry subset overlaps with national 2012 data in row 9. Do not sum with national row for same period.

source: WHO Multi-country Cholera Situation Report 2024 AFRO
processing_notes: Source states: WHO AFRO weekly bulletin March 2024 confirms Guinea not listed among 13 countries with active cholera transmission.
